data.narrative:
Figure AI, a Series C artificial intelligence and software company founded by Brett Adcock, is evaluated against a comparable universe of three same-stage private peers in the AI & Software sector, supplemented by a broader set of nine private companies and one public comparable (Palantir). The company has raised over $1.0 billion to date.

The peer-median method is the applicable valuation approach. Three same-sector, same-stage comparables—Skild AI ($14.0B), Crusoe Energy ($10.0B), and Together AI ($8.3B)—yield a median valuation of $10.0B, with a range spanning $8.3B to $14.0B. The stage-progression method was inapplicable because the reported post-money valuation of $39B implies a valuation-to-capital-raised multiple exceeding 20x, which substantially exceeds reasonable bounds for a Series C company and suggests a data integrity issue in the funding-tracker source.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $8.5B to $11.5B, centered on the peer median of $10.0B. Key uncertainties include the limited peer sample size (three direct comparables) and the wide dispersion within that set, which reflects heterogeneity in stage, technology maturity, and capital efficiency across the AI sector. A more robust valuation would require additional same-stage private market transactions or a meaningful public market baseline to cross-validate the peer median result.
